items.title: Episil says SiC capacity utilisation rebounded to ~90% from ~30% in H1 2026
items.text: DIGITIMES reports Episil chairman Rex Hsu saying overall demand has gradually recovered, with SiC capacity utilisation up from about 30% in the first half of 2026 to about 90% now, with AI demand cited as a driver. Only the lede was accessible (paywalled). It points to a demand upturn at a Taiwan foundry, though substrate price deflation remains a risk for new Indian entrants.

sources.title: AI demand drives Episil SiC V-shaped recovery as GaN and TVS capacity reaches full utilization

items.title: Wolfspeed gets conditional US$1.5bn, 30-year US DoW loan commitment for SiC and GaN
items.text: Wolfspeed announced a conditional commitment letter from the US Department of War's Office of Strategic Capital for up to $1.5 billion of long-term senior secured delayed-draw term financing over 30 years, with warrants for up to 7.5% of fully diluted equity. Funding is conditional on due diligence, definitive agreements and approvals, and Wolfspeed says there is no assurance it will be provided. For India, it signals state-backed Western capacity in SiC substrates and devices, a competitive benchmark for RIR and L&T Semiconductor's fabless approach.

items.title: Wolfspeed jumps 16.30% to $36.25 after 200mm SiC substrate launch
items.text: Wolfspeed shares rose 16.30% to close at $36.25 (+$5.08) in New York on 2 Oct 2026, after it introduced new premium power substrates in its 200 mm silicon carbide portfolio. The report also cites rotation into specialty semiconductor names. It is a global read-across for sentiment on SiC materials; no direct listed Indian company is affected, and RIR and L&T remain early-stage in SiC.

items.title: Wolfspeed launches Premium 200mm n-type SiC substrate, orderable now
items.text: Wolfspeed introduced a Premium 200mm n-type SiC substrate with fewer than 0.01 micropipes per square centimetre (under three per wafer), saying its 200mm operations have been in continuous production since 2022. It is aimed at higher-voltage, larger-die devices and better yields. For India's early SiC entrants such as RIR (epi) and L&T Semiconductor (fabless), it shows the quality bar set by incumbents.
